extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students in mathematical logic and computability theory
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook chapter exposition of definability, representability, and computability in a finitely axiomatized subtheory AE of arithmetic (Cn AE). Contains precise definitions (representability, numeralwise determination, recursive), key theorems (characterizations, closure properties), and worked examples (primes, divisibility, encoding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eventual periodicity characterization (Theorem 32F)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of natural numbers is definable in (N; 0, S, <, +) iff it is eventually periodic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof reduces definability to quantifier-free formulas in the language N≡ and shows atomic v1-only formulas yield finite, co-finite, or periodic sets; hence definability ⇔ eventual periodicity. Use least common multiple M of moduli and search M consecutive integers; add 0 lower bound to handle negative lower-bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication not definable (Corollary 32G)
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiplication relation {(m,n,p) | p = m·n in N} is not definable in (N; 0, S, <, +).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiplication were definable then the set of squares would be definable in (N; +) and thus eventually periodic, but the set of squares is not eventually periodic, contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set AE of axioms (definition of the subtheory AE)
rubrics_metrics.description: AE is the finite set of eleven sentences: S1, S2 (successor axioms), L1–L3 (ordering axioms), A1–A2 (addition recursion), M1–M2 (multiplication recursion), E1–E2 (exponentiation recursion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These axioms give recursion equations for +, ·, E and basic ordering facts; AE is chosen as a finitely axiomatizable subtheory of Th N strong enough to represent decidable relations. AE proves many numerals and ordering facts used later (e.g., AE proves which numbers are < Sk0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of representability in a theory T
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ρ (with only v1,..,vm free) represents an m-ary relation R in a theory T iff for every a1,..,am in N: (1) if (a1,..,am) ∈ R then ρ(Sa1 0,..,Sam 0) ∈ T, and (2) if (a1,..,am) ∉ R then ¬ρ(Sa1 0,..,Sam 0) ∈ T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the semantic notion of definability (truth in N) by a deductive notion (provability from axioms). Representability requires that T decide each numeral instance of ρ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeralwise determination by AE
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ϕ (with only v1,..,vm free) is numeralwise determined by AE iff for every tuple (a1,..,am) either AE ⊢ ϕ(Sa1 0,..,Sam 0) or AE ⊢ ¬ϕ(Sa1 0,..,Sam 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeralwise determination is the syntactic property used to lift a semantic definition in N to representability in Cn AE; theorem 33E leverages this condition. Theorem 33I provides closure properties to help prove numeralwise determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of representability in Cn AE (Theorem 33E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ρ represents a relation R in Cn AE iff (1) ρ is numeralwise determined by AE, and (2) ρ defines R in N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that N is a model of AE: if ρ represents R in Cn AE then both conditions hold trivially. Conversely, if ρ defines R in N and AE decides every numeral instance of ρ, then AE proves exactly the correct instances, hence ρ represents R in Cn AE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability implies decidability (Theorem 33F and Corollary 33G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is representable in a consistent axiomatizable theory T then R is decidable. In particular, any relation representable in a consistent finitely axiomatizable theory is decidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate theorems of T effectively; for given tuple, search the enumeration until either ρ(S...) or ¬ρ(S...) appears. Consistency ensures the first appearance yields the correct membership answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of recursive relation
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation R on N is recursive iff it is representable in some consistent finitely axiomatizable theory (in a language with 0 and S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the chosen precise formal counterpart to the informal notion of 'decidable relation' in the textbook. Under Church's thesis, recursion coincides with decidability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church's Thesis (informal principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The assertion that the informal notion 'decidable' corresponds exactly to the formal notion 'recursive' (i.e., representability in consistent finitely axiomatizable theories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not a mathematical theorem but a strongly supported identification: all reasonable formalizations (Turing machines, register machines) yield the same class of relations. The book accepts Church's thesis for further exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of computable function
rubrics_metrics.description: A function f: N^k → N is computable iff there is an effective procedure that, given any k-tuple of natural numbers (presented as numerals), will produce f of that tuple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computability is the function-analogue of decidability. Practical resource bounds are ignored; this is an idealized notion. Addition and multiplication are computable by standard algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence for computability (Theorem 33H)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a function f: N^k → N the following are equivalent: (a) f is computable; (b) the graph of f is a decidable relation; (c) the graph of f is effectively (recursively) enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketches: (a)⇒(b) compute f and compare; (b)⇒(c) enumerate tuples and filter; (c)⇒(a) search enumeration for tuple starting with inputs to extract output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeralwise determination closure (Theorem 33I)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Any atomic formula is numeralwise determined by AE. (b) If ϕ and ψ are numeralwise determined then so are ¬ϕ and ϕ→ψ. (c) If ϕ is numeralwise determined then bounded quantifications ∀x(x<y→ϕ) and ∃x(x<y∧ϕ) are numeralwise determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem is the main tool for proving many natural relations are representable: show a formula defines the relation in N and that AE decides all numeral instances. Example: the primes are represented by a bounded-quantifier formula and thus numeralwise determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional representation definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ϕ(v1,..,vm+1) functionally represents an m-place function f in Cn AE iff for every a1,..,am, AE ⊢ ∀vm+1[ϕ(Sa1 0,..,Sam 0, vm+1) ↔ vm+1 = S^{f(a1,..,am)}0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional representation asserts both existence (←) and uniqueness (→) of the output; the uniqueness clause is essential to lift a relational representation to an actual function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional representation implies relational representation (Theorem 33J)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ functionally represents f in Cn AE then ϕ also represents f when viewed as a relation (i.e., AE proves the right membership and non-membership instances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate because the biconditional gives both the positive instance (existence) and the refutability of wrong outputs (uniqueness), yielding AE ⊢ ϕ(Sa0, Sb0) iff f(a)=b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing functional representation from relational (Theorem 33K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a formula θ that represents f as a relation in Cn AE, one can build a formula ϕ(v1,v2) := θ(v1,v2) ∧ ∀z(z<v2 → ¬θ(v1,z)) that functionally represents f (i.e., enforces uniqueness) in Cn AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction appends a minimality/uniqueness clause asserting no smaller witness exists; proof uses AE theorems about numeral-bounded orderings to derive uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equational representability of simple functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an m-place function f is given by an equation vm+1 = t where t is a term using only v1..vm, then that equation defines a function in N and is numeralwise determined by AE, hence functionally represents f. Examples: successor v2 = Sv1, constants vm+1 = Sb0, projections vm+1 = vi, addition v3 = v1 + v2, multiplication v3 = v1·v2, exponentiation v3 = v1 E v2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every representable function has such a direct equational form, but many basic arithmetic functions do. The quantifier-free equivalence in N yields AE-proofs for numeral instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under composition (Theorem 33L)
rubrics_metrics.description: The class of functions representable in Cn AE is closed under composition: if g is n-place and h1,..,hn are m-place representable functions, then f(a)=g(h1(a),..,hn(a)) is representable and a formula can be built from the representing formulas for g and the hi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct ϕ using universal or existential quantification over intermediate yi: e.g. ∀y1..∀yn(θ1→..→θn→ψ) or ∃y1..∃yn(θ1∧..∧θn∧ψ); AE-provable biconditionals for the components yield the biconditional for f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under least-zero (μ-) operator (Theorem 33M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If g(a1,..,am,b) is representable and for every a there exists some b with g(a,b)=0, then the function f(a) = least b such that g(a,b)=0 (f = μb[g(...)=0]) is representable in Cn AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalize 'g(a,b)=0 and for all c<b, g(a,c)≠0' by a formula ψ(v1,v2,0) ∧ ∀y(y<v2 → ¬ψ(v1,y,0)); numeralwise determination (bounded quantification) yields representability of the least-zero function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalog: closure properties and example representable relations/functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantifier-free definable relations are representable; representable relations closed under union, intersection, complement. Characteristic function KR is representable iff R is representable. If R is representable and f,g are representable functions, then the relation {(a) | (f(a),g(a))∈R} is representable. Specific examples: divisibility, the set of primes, and pairs of adjacent primes are representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Theorem 33I and previous closure theorems. Divisibility: a divides b iff exists q≤b with a·q=b (quantifier-free kernel + bounded quantification). Primes and adjacent primes formalized with bounded quantifiers and ordering facts provable in AE.
